color.why: X fully honors the warm graphite palette with strict brass discipline and implements the signature Projected Light Rule behind the featured render frame; Y removes the off-palette colors and passes contrast but completely omits the projected light spill cue.

typography.why: X achieves flawless typographical hierarchy adhering strictly to DESIGN.md tokens (520-weight display title, 560-weight 15px section titles, Geist Mono strictly for data) and enforces clean sentence case; Y maintains good font roles but defaults to Title Case and lacks the subtle display polish of X.

layout.why: X establishes a clear visual hierarchy with one prominent primary action, a featured latest render frame, and a steady 52px velvet band; Y lacks any primary button in the header, duplicates room navigation between the sticky band and the body, and inflates the band to 100px on mobile viewports.

accessibility.why: Both contestants drastically improve accessibility to zero critical or serious axe violations, provide brass focus-visible rings, replace emoji divs with semantic interactive elements, and provide proper form labels and error handling.

states.why: X delivers flawless layout continuity across ready, empty, and loading states, with an interactive Try Again simulation and calm inline delete confirmation; Y's Try Again button permanently traps the user in an infinite loading skeleton with no resolution, and its empty state discards the room cards grid.

copy.why: Both outputs faithfully align with PRODUCT.md by eliminating the pipeline render button in favor of agent asks, correcting Finder casing, and explaining that Desk files are optional; X has a slight edge on sentence case and stage line clarity but under the 1.0 margin threshold.

motion.why: Both remove the 1.5s staggered overshoot and scale(1.1) hovers in favor of projector-eased transitions with prefers-reduced-motion considerations; X uses compositor-friendly skeleton sweeps while Y guards transforms with no-preference media queries.

ux.why: X captures the true soul of Creative Room Desk as a dark screening room where the samples carry the light, providing an immediate visual hero in the latest render and a clear primary action ('Ask for a render') that routes work to agents; Y feels like a generic administrative list without a visual focal point or clear header CTA.

X: Loading skeleton sweep animation runs on 15 elements concurrently when reduced motion is not active (X/index.html:208, X/shots/metrics.jsonl:3).
Y: Error state recovery is broken: clicking 'Try again' triggers setState('loading') which permanently hangs on the loading skeleton with no timer or return mechanism (Y/index.html:1007).
Header actions row has no primary action button, showing only secondary 'Open in Finder' and ghost 'Delete piece' (Y/index.html:840-843).
Sticky velvet band height expands to 100px on viewports under 1024px due to wrapping room tabs onto a second row, consuming excessive vertical viewport space on mobile (Y/index.html:678-687).
Redundant room navigation renders room links twice consecutively (once as sticky band tabs, and immediately again as card links in the main content) (Y/index.html:796-805, 860-865).

overall.why: X captures the authentic screening-room identity of Creative Room Desk by showcasing the latest render with the signature Projected Light Rule and providing a clear primary action that connects directly to the agent workflow. Its state transitions and layout continuity are rock-solid, maintaining a compact 52px band and flawless responsive balance on mobile. In contrast, Y lacks a primary header CTA, breaks error recovery with a permanent loading freeze, and clutters narrow viewports with a 100px double-height sticky band.
